headline: Q1/Q2 hardening: streaming reliability, enterprise auth/transport, and tool-calling pipeline
body:
Three parallel workstreams are landing this cycle, all classified as substantial (effort 8) cross-cutting fixes rather than isolated patches.

Streaming (Q1, no dependencies): we're fixing provider-proxied SSE parsing so streams that omit the standard 'event:' field (e.g. Anthropic via Bedrock proxy) don't hard-fail with zero generation chunks. Structured-output streaming (with_structured_output) will stop emitting spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and stop dropping response metadata/headers like x-request-id. disable_streaming='tool_calling' currently crashes with an AttributeError (an AsyncStream passed where a ChatCompletion is expected) and, even when it doesn't crash, disables streaming globally instead of scoping to tool-calling turns only — both are being fixed. Agent/graph paths that call ainvoke internally instead of astream (so on_llm_new_token never fires despite graph-level streaming being enabled) are being routed through astream. We're also fixing a known-incorrect assertion in the core streaming error-callback test suite and shoring up standard test coverage/release sequencing for tool-call streaming across integration packages. Flag if you depend on the current global-disable behavior of disable_streaming — that's a deliberate behavior change.

Authentication (Q1, no dependencies): ChatAnthropic is getting custom HTTP client support with mTLS for corporate proxy/PKI setups. MCP tool discovery's auth header/token forwarding is being fixed to eliminate spurious 403s on correctly-configured credentials. AzureChatOpenAI and BaseChatOpenAI are moving toward a shared httpx client/connection-pooling layer to remove redundant connection/auth setup — this is a refactor touching integrations that were built independently, so regression risk in existing auth flows is real. Separately, SSRF/allowlist host validation is being hardened to close a bypass via environment-based auth checks; this is flagged high-risk for breaking legitimate enterprise configs that currently rely on env-based checks to reach internal hosts, so scoping here matters.

Tool-calling (Q2, no dependencies): scope includes Gemini-style strict provider validation (turn-order/thought-signature) rejecting injected tool-call history; graceful handling of malformed/fragmented streamed tool-call payloads instead of crashes or silent wrong-tool execution; not forcing tool_choice='required' for reasoning/thinking models that only support 'auto'/'none'; closing the gap where ToolNode can execute a human-rejected tool call (safety-critical, flagged high risk if the fix is incomplete); adding tool_call_id to on_tool_start/on_tool_end events for parallel-call attribution; proactive tool-call-limit warnings before the limit is hit; and unifying handle_tool_error/ToolException behavior across @tool, ToolNode, and wrap_tool_call middleware.
call_to_action: Review the disable_streaming and SSRF/allowlist sections for behavior-change risk in your area, and flag any code paths you own that depend on the current (buggy) global-disable or env-based-auth-bypass behavior before those fixes merge.

key_claims.text: Provider-proxied SSE streams that omit the 'event:' field (e.g., Anthropic via Bedrock proxy) cause hard failures with no generation chunks.
Streaming with with_structured_output produces spurious Pydantic serializer warnings and drops response metadata/headers like x-request-id.

disable_streaming='tool_calling' crashes with an AttributeError (AsyncStream passed where ChatCompletion expected) and, even when not crashing, disables streaming globally instead of scoping to tool-calling turns.
Agent/graph execution paths call ainvoke instead of astream internally, so on_llm_new_token never fires even when graph-level streaming is enabled.
There is a known-incorrect assertion in the core streaming error-callback test suite, and gaps in standard test coverage/release sequencing for tool-call streaming across integration packages.
ChatAnthropic lacks support for custom HTTP clients and mTLS, blocking corporate proxy/PKI authentication.
MCP tool discovery fails to forward auth headers/tokens consistently, causing 403 errors despite correctly configured credentials.
AzureChatOpenAI and BaseChatOpenAI do not share connection/auth setup, creating redundant connection overhead and inconsistent behavior; a shared httpx client/connection-pooling layer is planned.

SSRF/allowlist host validation can be bypassed via environment-based auth checks, and hardening this risks breaking legitimate enterprise configs that rely on env-based checks to reach internal hosts.
Strict-validation providers like Gemini reject injected precomputed tool-call history due to turn-order/thought-signature rules.
Malformed or fragmented streamed tool-call payloads can crash the pipeline or cause silent execution of the wrong tool.
Agents unconditionally force tool_choice='required', which breaks reasoning/thinking models that only support 'auto' or 'none'.
A human-rejected tool call can still be executed by ToolNode because rejection enforcement is not reliably wired into execution.
tool_call_id is missing from on_tool_start (and reportedly on_tool_end) streaming events, preventing attribution of streamed output to specific tool calls in parallel execution.
Tool-call limits are enforced only after the fact, with no proactive warning as the limit approaches.
ToolException raised inside wrap_tool_call middleware is not caught properly at the agent level, and handle_tool_error behaves differently between @tool decorator and ToolNode.
Streaming and authentication roadmap items are both scheduled Q1 with no dependencies; tool-calling is scheduled Q2 with no dependencies.
